detailed_rationale:
Anupam Rasayan is a specialty-chemicals manufacturer across agrochemicals (65% of FY24 revenue), personal care (17%) and pharmaceuticals (9%) verticals. The quant model's growth-divergence flag is well founded: trailing one-year revenue growth of 64.5% sits far above the three-year (13.9%) and even five-year (24%) CAGRs, and screener's own automated analysis explicitly flags this as likely reflecting 'acquisition/one-off factors rather than organic growth' - fixed assets jumped from Rs.2,185cr to Rs.3,713cr year-on-year (a ~70% increase), indicating the recent revenue jump (Rs.1,437cr to Rs.2,365cr) is substantially a function of new capacity coming online rather than a genuine demand step-change. This is exactly the base-effect/capex-ramp pattern the analyst process is meant to catch rather than credit at face value.

More concerning than the growth-quality question is the deterioration in working-capital efficiency: the cash-conversion cycle has stretched from 111 days to 377 days (Mar 2024 to Mar 2026), with debtor days at 148 and inventory sitting at 490 days - an extreme build-up that could reflect either genuine forward-inventory positioning ahead of new long-term supply contracts (there is a non-binding letter of intent with BASQUEVOLT for a $300 million, 10-year battery-materials supply relationship) or, more worryingly, slow-moving stock and weaker-than-expected offtake. A further anomaly is the effective tax rate dropping to 0-13% from a historical ~30%, which we cannot fully explain from available sources but flag as worth scrutiny (a genuine SEZ/backward-area tax holiday tied to new capacity is plausible, but the scale of the drop warrants a closer look).

Reverse-DCF: at 81-84x trailing earnings against ROE of just 6-7% and a quality percentile near the bottom of the universe, the market is pricing this as a hypergrowth story. Given that a large share of recent growth looks like a capex/base-effect artifact rather than organic demand, and working capital is stretching in a way that raises real cash-conversion questions, we do not believe the current multiple is supported by the underlying return profile.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model scores this Sell on both the 3-year (37.8) and 1-year (39.0) composites despite the eye-catching 1-year revenue growth print, because the quality score (weak ROE/ROCE) and rich value score pull the composite down regardless. Having confirmed the growth print is substantially a capex/base-effect artifact rather than a durable acceleration, and flagged the working-capital deterioration and tax-rate anomaly, we see no basis to rescue and confirm Sell.
summary: Anupam Rasayan's headline 65% revenue growth looks impressive but appears to be substantially a base-effect from a large recent capacity expansion rather than a genuine demand step-change, and the underlying cash-conversion cycle has stretched dramatically (111 to 377 days) alongside a low, roughly 6-7% return on equity. At 81-84 times trailing earnings, we do not see this rich a multiple justified by the underlying return and cash-conversion profile, and recommend keeping this a Sell.
positive_para: Anupam Rasayan operates in structurally growing specialty-chemicals end-markets (agrochemicals, personal care, pharma intermediates) and has been investing heavily in new capacity (fixed assets up about 70% year-on-year), with a forward-looking, if non-binding, $300 million 10-year supply relationship signed with BASQUEVOLT in battery materials that could open a genuinely new growth vertical if it converts to a binding contract.
negative_para: Return on equity remains weak at 6-7%, well below what an 81-84x earnings multiple would typically demand, and the reported 65% one-year revenue growth appears substantially driven by new capacity coming online rather than organic demand - screener's own automated analysis flags this base-effect concern directly. The cash-conversion cycle has stretched alarmingly from 111 to 377 days, with inventory sitting at 490 days, and the effective tax rate has dropped unexplained from a historical ~30% to 0-13%, both of which raise real earnings-quality questions.
reverse_dcf_judgment: An 81-84x multiple against 6-7% ROE implies the market is crediting the full 65% headline growth rate as durable and organic; our read is that a meaningful share of that growth reflects new capacity ramping rather than demand pull, so we would apply a materially lower growth assumption than the trailing print, at which point the current multiple looks difficult to justify.
